ai.literal: Greatness-yielding wealth even if obtained, to others harm not doing [is] blemish-without-those's principle.
ai.translation: Even if it brings wealth that yields greatness, not doing harm to others is the firm principle of the flawless.
ai.modern: சிறப்பைத் தரும் செல்வத்தைப் பெறுவதாக இருந்தாலும், மற்றவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே குற்றமற்றவர்களின் கொள்கையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core principle of those who are free from moral blemishes. It states that they will never cause harm to others, even if doing so would bring them immense wealth and greatness. The phrase 'மாசற்றார் கோள்' (the resolve of the flawless) emphasizes that true purity lies in the absolute refusal to do harm. The contrast between 'சிறப்பீனும் செல்வம்' (wealth yielding greatness) and 'இன்னா செய்யாமை' (not doing harm) highlights that no material or social gain can ever justify inflicting pain on others.

ai.literal: Having been angry harm done even when, in return harm not doing [is] blemish-less ones' principle.
ai.translation: Even when others do harm out of anger, it is the principle of the flawless not to do harm in return.
ai.modern: மற்றவர்கள் சினந்து துன்பம் செய்தாலும், அவர்களுக்குத் திரும்பத் துன்பம் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே குற்றமற்றவர்களின் கொள்கையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core principle of those who are free from moral flaws. It states that even when someone harms them out of pure anger, they must not retaliate. The word 'kaṟuttu' emphasizes that the harm was done with deliberate anger, making it harder to forgive. Yet, 'maṟuttu' (in return) and 'ceyyāmai' (not doing) show that breaking the cycle of harm is the true mark of the flawless.

ai.literal: Without doing, even to those who harmed, painful things after doing, inescapable sorrow it will give.
ai.translation: If you do harm in return, even to those who harmed you without provocation, it will bring you inescapable sorrow.
ai.modern: நாம் எந்தத் தீங்கும் செய்யாமல் இருக்க, நமக்குத் தீங்கு செய்தவர்களுக்கும் நாம் துன்பம் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்தால், அது நாம் தப்ப முடியாத பெருந்துன்பத்தை நமக்குத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against retaliation, even when the initial harm was completely unprovoked. The phrase 'செய்யாமல் செற்றார்' refers to those who cause harm without any prior offense from the victim. If one responds to such unprovoked hostility by doing 'இன்னாத' (painful things), the result is 'உய்யா விழுமம்'—a sorrow so deep that one cannot escape or survive it. The word 'உய்யா' means 'unable to escape', emphasizing that revenge ultimately destroys the one who takes it, trapping them in an endless cycle of suffering.

ai.literal: Harm those-who-did punishing they to-feel-ashamed good-kindness having-done leaving.
ai.translation: The true way to punish those who have harmed you is to do them a good deed that makes them feel ashamed, and then let it go.
ai.modern: தமக்குத் துன்பம் செய்தவரைத் தண்டிக்கும் சிறந்த வழி, அவர் வெட்கப்படும்படி அவருக்கு ஒரு நன்மையைச் செய்து அந்தப் பகையை மறந்துவிடுவதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet redefines the concept of punishment for a wrongdoer. Instead of seeking revenge, the victim is advised to respond with unexpected kindness. This good deed will make the offender feel deep shame for their actions, which serves as the true punishment. Finally, the victim must let go of the incident entirely, freeing themselves from the cycle of harm.

ai.literal: Is there a result from knowledge, in the state of not regarding another's pain like one's own pain?
ai.translation: What is the benefit of knowledge if one does not regard the pain of others as one's own?
ai.modern: பிறருடைய துன்பத்தைத் தன் துன்பம் போலக் கருதிப் போற்றாவிட்டால், ஒருவன் பெற்ற அறிவினால் ஆகும் பயன் உண்டோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the ultimate purpose of acquiring knowledge. It asserts that true wisdom must naturally lead to empathy and compassion. If a person cannot recognize and treat the suffering of others just as they would their own, their intelligence yields no meaningful benefit. The word 'கடை' here acts as a conditional, meaning 'in the state where' or 'if'.

ai.literal: Painful things as oneself things-understood not-approaching is-needed another-upon doing.
ai.translation: One must avoid doing to others the things that one has personally felt to be painful.
ai.modern: தனக்குத் துன்பம் தருபவை என்று தான் அனுபவித்து உணர்ந்த செயல்களை, மற்றவர்களுக்குச் செய்யாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes a universal principle of empathy based on personal experience. It states that if a person has felt certain actions to be painful, they should recognize that those same actions will hurt others. The word உணர்ந்தவை emphasizes this personal realization of pain. Therefore, one must strictly avoid inflicting such deeds upon anyone else.

ai.literal: However much even, at any time, to anyone, with the mind which is, ignoble things non-doing is foremost.
ai.translation: The foremost virtue is to never intentionally do anything ignoble to anyone, at any time, to any extent.
ai.modern: எக்காலத்திலும், எவருக்கும், எவ்வளவு சிறிய அளவிலும், மனதறிந்து எந்த ஒரு தீங்கையும் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே முதன்மையான அறமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest principle of non-harming. It emphasizes that one should not commit even the smallest ignoble act against anyone at any time. The phrase 'மனத்தான் ஆம்' stresses that this restraint must be intentional and conscious, making the deliberate avoidance of harm the foremost of all virtues.

ai.literal: one's own - to life - painfulness - oneself - he who knows - why - indeed - abiding - to lives - harmful things - doing
ai.translation: Why does a person who knows what is painful to his own life inflict harm upon other living beings?
ai.modern: தன் உயிருக்குத் துன்பம் தருபவை எவை என்று உணர்ந்தவன், மற்ற உயிர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்வது ஏனோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the contradiction in human behavior where a person harms others despite knowing how pain feels. The phrase 'தன் உயிர்க்கு இன்னாமை தான் அறிவான்' refers to someone who has personally experienced and understood what causes suffering to their own life. 'மன் உயிர்க்கு' refers to the abiding community of other living beings. The poet asks 'என் கொலோ' (why indeed) such a person would commit 'இன்னா செயல்' (harmful deeds) against others, highlighting that true empathy should naturally prevent us from inflicting the pain we ourselves dread.

ai.literal: To others harm forenoon if one does, to oneself harm afternoon of themselves will come.
ai.translation: If one does harm to others in the morning, harm will come to them of its own accord in the afternoon.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் மற்றவர்களுக்குக் காலையில் துன்பம் செய்தால், அவருக்கான துன்பம் மாலையில் தானாகவே வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns about the swift and inevitable return of harmful actions. If a person inflicts pain on others in the early part of the day, pain will naturally seek them out later in the same day. The contrasting words for forenoon and afternoon emphasize that the consequences of evil actions return very quickly, without waiting for another lifetime. The word 'tāmē' (of themselves) shows that this retribution is an automatic, inescapable law of nature.

ai.literal: Pain all pain those-who-did upon will-become pain they-will-not-do pain absence those-who-desire.
ai.translation: All suffering falls back upon those who caused it. Therefore, those who desire a life free of suffering will not inflict pain on others.
ai.modern: பிறருக்குத் துன்பம் செய்தவர்களுக்கே எல்லாத் துன்பங்களும் வந்து சேரும். அதனால் தமக்குத் துன்பம் வரக்கூடாது என்று விரும்புபவர்கள் பிறருக்குத் துன்பம் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet establishes a direct consequence for causing harm: all the pain one inflicts will eventually return to fall upon them. The word 'நோய்' (nōy) is used repeatedly here to mean pain or suffering rather than physical disease. Because suffering inevitably rebounds on the wrongdoer, a logical conclusion is drawn in the second line. Those who wish for an absence of suffering in their own lives will carefully avoid inflicting pain on others.
